name: Khatti Dal
subtitle: everyday toor dal made unapologetically sour with tamarind

ingredients.qty: 200g, rinsed until the water runs clear

ingredients.note: use a compounded-free asafoetida to keep the dish gluten-free

prepNotes: Soak the toor dal 20 minutes if you have the time — it cooks softer and faster.
Soak the tamarind in hot water for 20 minutes, squeeze it out with your fingers and strain; the dal should be assertively sour, not merely tangy.
Most block asafoetida is cut with wheat flour, so buy a compounded-free one if gluten matters to you.

steps.text: Pressure cook the dal with the turmeric, chopped tomato, green chillies and 700ml water for 4 whistles, about 12 minutes.
Let the pressure fall on its own, then whisk the dal hard for 30 seconds until it is smooth and creamy with no whole lentils left.
steps.tip: Whisking, not blending — a blender makes it gluey.

steps.text: Return the pan to a low flame, add the remaining water and salt, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Stir in the tamarind water and simmer 8 minutes, until the raw sour smell has cooked off and the dal has thickened slightly.
steps.tip: Taste after these 8 minutes, not before — tamarind mellows as it cooks.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a small pan for the tempering. Crackle the mustard seeds, then the cumin and fenugreek.
Add the crushed garlic and fry until it turns golden, about 1 minute, then the dried red chillies, curry leaves and asafoetida. It will spit hard.
steps.tip: Take the pan off the heat before the asafoetida goes in — it scorches in seconds.

steps.text: If using onion, add it to the tempering and fry 3 minutes until soft and translucent.
Pour the tempering into the dal, cover immediately for a minute to trap the aroma, then stir through.
Finish with coriander leaves and serve with plain rice and a wedge of lime.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. It sets firm when cold — reheat with 100ml water per portion, stirring until it flows again, and refresh with a small second tempering if it tastes flat.
